data.title: Reflections on Sudoku, or the Impossibility of Systematizing Thought
data.author: rjpower9000
data.article_summary:
本文反思了在解决编程问题（如数独求解器）时的思维过程，并联系到**Entscheidungsproblem**（决策问题）。作者讨论了在编程和写作中面临的挑战，即如何在动手编码或写作前充分思考问题空间，而不至于过早陷入细节。作者提出了“10%规则”，即在开始编码前花10%的时间思考问题，以避免过早迷失方向。

作者进一步探讨了是否能系统化思维过程，提到即便像陶哲轩这样的数学家也无法解决所有问题。他得出结论，思维无法完全系统化，每个人依赖不同的思维工具，且这些工具可通过学习改进。

文章还比较了**Ron Jeffries**和**Peter Norvig**在数独求解器开发中的不同方法。Jeffries采用测试驱动开发（TDD），但过程冗长且效果不佳；Norvig则通过高层次分析和有效数据结构，迅速找到解决方案。作者认为Norvig的方法更系统，但他也承认Norvig在相关领域有丰富经验。

最终，作者对TDD持保留态度，认为测试无法解决“知道该做什么”的根本问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的设计与问题解决方法，包括TDD（测试驱动开发）、系统化思维以及创造性解决问题的方式。

不同观点：
• **[mbb70]** 支持Rich Hickey的观点，认为良好的设计不是自然从好的编程中产生的，背景和领域知识至关重要。他强调在设计前需要深思熟虑，并借鉴他人的经验。
  
• **[JonChesterfield]** 引用了另一篇文章，将TDD描述为从简单的起点向解决方案递增搜索的过程，认为这种方法在路径平滑可微的情况下有效，但对复杂问题可能不适用。

• **[andrewlgood]** 将TDD与Six Sigma等质量改进工具对比，指出这些工具能帮助识别问题，但不能直接提供解决方案，强调头脑风暴等创造性方法的重要性。

• **[gchamonlive]** 对必须找到通用问题解决方法的观念提出质疑，认为接受并拥抱问题的复杂性和创造性过程是重要的，不必强求立即解决所有问题或追求生产力。

• **[schoen]** 提出软件正确性的问题通常是突变的，而不是连续的，因此通过迭代改进找到正确解决方案可能不现实，特别是在算法问题中。

• **[rjpower9000]** 反思TDD和系统化思维的局限性，认为思想无法完全系统化，并对此感到不满意。

• **[awanderingmind]** 赞赏对不同编程方法的具体分析，认为文章在指出某一方法的不足时没有过度泛化。

• **[taeric]** 指出在其他领域也存在类似情况，某些不受欢迎的技术可能比公认的成功技术更有效，如大纲、任务分解、对象建模和死记硬背。

• **[prmph]** 认为人工智能无法完全替代人类思维和技能，即使是简单的CRUD应用程序的开发也无法完全系统化。

• **[fydorm]** 提到刚读过Norvig关于Sudoku的文章，认为当前讨论与之相关，增加了讨论的趣味性。

• **[IceDane]** 批评Ron Jeffries的文章，认为其教条化且不自知，强调教条不适用于所有情况。

• **[groby_b]** 详细分析了TDD和决策问题，指出可以通过特定程序和任务的测试来验证解决方案，但对于更复杂的问题需要更高层次的形式化约束设计。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了TDD的适用范围，特别是在复杂算法和软件正确性问题中的局限性。
• 强调了创造性和背景知识在解决问题中的重要性，质疑系统化方法的万能性。
• 不同评论者对是否需要通用问题解决方法存在争议，部分认为应接受问题的复杂性和不确定性。
• 技术工具和方法的价值被多方讨论，强调了在具体情境中选择合适方法的重要性。

Reflections on Sudoku, Or the Impossibility of Systematizing Thought
I reflect on the Entscheidungsproblem how it relates to Sudoku solvers. It's a little weird.
.
The other day, to no one's surprise, I was fumbling over a programming problem.
This wasn't anything satisfyingly algorithmic, but more the thing where you're
evaluating a million questions on "how should I structure this system?". While
I'm no design purist, I like to at least make an attempt at sketching out the
problem space and think through options before I just start coding something. My
rule of thumb for this is, let's call it the "10% rule" - make sure I try to
think hard about a problem for 10% of the time before I start playing around
with code. Writing code helps clarify many things but it's also easy to get
stuck in local minima
I have the same problem when writing text, like this blog post. Put me in front of an editor and I'll pointlessly recraft sentences instead of getting the thing finished.
. This rule helps keep me from getting lost too early,
but I often think about whether I could do better.
I'd like to say I have a systematic process I apply here. I don't. I think
over one idea, then another,
writing down my thoughts
,
but it's always hard to feel like you're making a lot of progress.
It's honestly frustrating. I often wish I could "systematize" it somehow,
applying some rigorous method and march towards the solution. Could I become one of
those
magic people
who just sit down in front of a problem and watch it decompose in front
of them?
Over time I've accepted that is impossible. There is no person, no process,
which can systematize thought. Millions of math problems
elude
Terence Tao
despite his brilliance.
Now I see these differences in aptitude as having different sets of
mental tools at your disposal. The more tools you have, the better tools you
have, and the better you are at applying them, then the better you get at
certain problems. Maybe your background makes you better or more interested in
different tools. But we can all learn new tools, and get better at the ones we
have.
This is all kind of murky and unsatisfying though. Wouldn't it be nice if you
just had a general method you could apply to solve everything? What happens if
you
think
you have a method to solve all problems?
The Sudoku Affair
A few months ago I read Zach Tellman's fascinating article on the
Sudoku
Affair
, in which he revisited Peter Norvig & Ron
Jeffries very, very different attempts to produce a workable Sudoku solver. (I
highly recommend reading the original article as well, as Zach's deep analysis
of Ron Jeffries attempts at producing a Sudoku solver is fascinating).
Some background: Ron Jeffries made a career advocating for test-driven
development (TDD) and extreme programming. Peter Norvig is a research lead at
Google and author of many papers and a few books on AI. As you'd expect, this
leads to different approaches to problems.
Ron Jeffries attempted to solve Sudoku by approaching it
"rigorously"
No offense intended, but just being clear this isn't like
mathematical rigour
but more of an applied philosophy.
from the perspective of TDD. He outlines the
problem, writes a test case and begins to iterate, adding tests and refactoring.
In the initial set of posts, he can't get to a real solution despite many hours
of effort. He then revisited the problem 20 years later, and in the end spends
50
posts
writing about the process of building a solver. At some point, he
finds code from another site
and starts to bring that into the fold. He eventually gets to a solution, though at
that point I honestly have trouble figuring out how much TDD had to do with the process.
Peter Norvig takes a different approach, analyzing the high-level problem and
then breaking down the data structures and outlining the solution in the course
of ~20 lines of code. While his code might be a bit dense to follow initially,
the way he approaches the problem and pre-builds data structures makes "testing"
trivial. His test for validity is part of the search condition for his program.
It's hard not to appreciate the systematic nature of Peter's approach: define
the problem, look through your toolkit, apply the relevant tools, success. Of
course, Peter has an advantage that he's
written
books
about related techniques.
Ron Jeffries attempt definitely didn't make me excited about TDD, I at least
respected that he didn't try to hide things after the fact.
Many people have commented about this over time, with lots to say
about TDD and programming. In Peter Siebel's post on
Unit testing in Coders at Work
even Peter Norvig chimes in, indicating he's not "anti-test", but that tests don't fix the
underlying issue of "knowing what to do."
Then bloggers were arguing back and forth about what this means. I don’t think
it means much of anything—I think test-driven design is great. I do that a lot
more than I used to do. But you can test all you want and if you don’t know how

data.title: Show HN: Tool-Assisted Speedrunning the Boring Parts of Animal Crossing (GCN)
data.author: hunterirving
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何使用Raspberry Pi Pico和GameCube键盘控制器来黑入游戏《动物森友会》（Animal Crossing），以提高游戏中打字速度和其他功能。项目包括：通过自定义键帽快速输入日记，循环播放喜爱的城镇音乐，解锁几乎所有物品，将任何图片或视频转换为游戏内的图案或动画，甚至在游戏中玩《贪吃蛇》。硬件部分需要Pi Pico、GameCube控制器延长线、电阻和二极管等组件，并提供了详细的组装步骤。软件部分涉及Python 3、ffmpeg等依赖项和多个构建脚本，用于快速开发和测试。项目源码遵循GPL-3.0许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《Animal Crossing》（动物森友会）相关黑客行为及其影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **对游戏黑客行为的赞赏**：
   - [mlaux] 和 [xp84] 表达了对在《Animal Crossing》上进行复杂黑客行为的支持和喜爱，认为这种行为不仅展现了黑客精神，还提升了游戏体验。特别是解决了原版游戏中使用操作系统键盘（OSK）输入繁琐的问题。
   - [dylan604] 认为这种黑客行为是一种极致且荒诞的时间投入，但充满创意，甚至让人不愿意玩原版游戏。

• **对黑客改进的幽默评价**：
   - [benrutter] 以幽默的方式描述了对黑客不断改进游戏功能的期待，从打字速度提升到图像上传功能，再到视频播放，甚至在游戏界面中玩另一款游戏，表现出对黑客创意潜力的认可。

• **对老游戏新功能的兴趣**：
   - [geoffpado] 虽然从未玩过初代《Animal Crossing》，但仍对在老游戏中加入质量提升的改进表示赞赏，认为这是在原硬件上运行老游戏的一种创新方式。

• **与其他游戏的比较**：
   - [hnlmorg] 提到自己使用类似的ASCII键盘玩《Phantasy Star Online》（梦幻之星在线），并指出即使在官方服务器关闭后，私人服务器依然活跃，表现出对其他老游戏社区活力的认可。

• **对游戏体验的反思**：
   - [dilDDoS] 表达了对《Animal Crossing》原版游戏的喜爱，但也指出其键盘输入方式已经显得过时，不如经过黑客改进后的版本流畅。

• **纯粹的喜爱表达**：
   - [agold97] 简单直接地表达了对《Animal Crossing》的热爱，没有涉及具体的技术或改进。

补充讨论：
• **对视频创作者的建议**：
   - [askl] 提到另一位YouTube创作者Hunter R.，并建议进行合作，显示出对相关内容创作者的关注和潜在合作的兴趣。

• **对特定黑客功能的调侃**：
   - [b0a04gl] 调侃了以1帧每秒（1fps）运行《贪吃蛇》游戏的忍耐力训练效果，表现出对某些极端技术改进的幽默反应。

争议的焦点：
• 争议不大，主要是对原版游戏键盘输入过时与否的看法存在分歧，部分人认为原版游戏的某些设计已经不再适应现代玩家需求，而其他人则单纯出于怀旧情感表达对游戏的喜爱。

pico-crossing
What if the GameCube Keyboard Controller worked with Animal Crossing...?
It started out as a "quick, simple project", then quickly turned into seven quick simple projects.
Demonstration video (on YouTube)
Typing at the speed of TAS
Typing in Animal Crossing (GCN) is painfully slow.
Or, at least.. it was. Not anymore.
Pro Gamer WPM (unassisted): TBD
Tool-assisted WPM: Also TBD
Custom Keycaps
Compose digital diary entries in style with this set of 81 custom, 3D printed keycaps that map perfectly to Animal Crossing's in-game character set.
See the separate
pico-crossing-keycaps
repository for FreeCAD project files and OBJ exports.
Infinite Playlist
Cycle through your favorite Town Tunes without having to futz about with e-Reader cards.
All Items Unlocked
Type the name of (almost) any item, and this little raccoon-looking guy will give it to you for free.
Usage: press
Shift
+
Alt
+
🗝️
, then type the name of any compatible item
Put any Image in the Game
Convert any image to display in Animal Crossing's pattern editor. The script automatically sets up a Python environment and handles all dependencies.
Basic usage:
./convert_image.sh monalisa.jpg
See
image_tools/README.md
for advanced usage.
Put any Video in the Game (if you're patient)
Convert videos to animated sequences in Animal Crossing (requires ffmpeg for video processing).
Basic usage:
./convert_video.sh rickroll.mp4
See
image_tools/README.md
for advanced usage.
A Playable Version of Snake... in Animal Crossing!?
It's more likely than you think.
Usage: press the
S
key while a design (image or video) is being entered.
Building the Hardware
You'll need:
a Raspberry Pi Pico (or Pi Pico W)
two GameCube controller extension cables
two 1k Ω resistors (1/4W or higher)
one 1N5817 Schottky diode (protects GameCube from USB 5V backfeeding during flashing/debugging)
Assembly:
Cut both extension cables and strip back the outer sleeve to reveal the 5 inner wires. You'll need two female plugs and one male plug.
Important:
Verify your extension cable pinouts before soldering! The colors in the provided schematic correspond to the "High Quality" labeled cables I used, but colors may vary between manufacturers or even batches.
Solder the components to the Pi according to the schematic:
Install the Schottky diode between the male plug's 5V line and the Pi's VSYS pin (cathode toward VSYS), then connect the 5V line from the male plug directly to the 5V lines on both of the female plugs.
Install pull-up resistors connecting the Pi's 3.3V supply to GPIO 3 and GPIO 4 on the Pi.
Connect the 3.3V line from the male plug directly to the 3.3v lines on both of the female plugs (without connecting it to the Pi).
Connect GND(POW) from the male plug to PIN 38 on the Pi and the GND(POW) lines on both of the female plugs.
Connect GND(SIG) from the male plug to PIN 3 on the Pi and the GND(SIG) lines on both of the female plugs.
Connect the DATA line from the male plug to GPIO 2 on the Pi. Connect the DATA lines from the female plugs to GPIO3 and GPIO4 on the Pi.
Prerequisites
System Dependencies
Python 3
- Required for image/video conversion tools
ffmpeg
- Required for video conversion (
brew install ffmpeg
on macOS)
picotool
- Required for flashing firmware to Pico
Raspberry Pi Pico SDK
- Set up according to official documentation
Installing picotool
macOS:
brew install picotool
Ubuntu/Debian:
sudo apt install picotool
Building the Software
This project includes several build scripts for different workflows:
Quick Build, Flash, and Monitor
For the fastest development cycle:
./buildflashmonitor.sh
This script runs build → flash → monitor in sequence. Great for testing changes.
Individual Build Scripts
Build only:
./build.sh
Cleans and builds the project, generating the .uf2 firmware file.
Flash only:
./flash.sh
Attempts to force the Pico into BOOTSEL mode and flash the firmware (no need to manually hold the BOOTSEL button).
Monitor serial output:
./monitor.sh
Opens a serial connection to view debug output from the Pico.

data.title: Show HN: McWig – A modal, Vim-like text editor written in Go
data.author: andrew_bbb
data.article_summary: McWig是一个由Go语言编写的模态文本编辑器，类似Vim，目前是早期开发阶段，主要用于编辑`.go`文件。它具备LSP自动补全、跳转定义、悬停信息、Tree-sitter支持、颜色主题、宏录制等功能，但存在较多漏洞。键位绑定大多模仿Vim，支持基本的代码编辑操作。项目初衷是快速探索文本编辑器的实现，未来计划发展为稳定、功能齐全的编辑器。当前仅为实验性项目，使用时需注意文件备份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个新的代码编辑器项目的功能、可用性、扩展性以及与Vim、Helix等已有编辑器的比较。

不同观点：
• [GuiShou] 认为该项目虽然是“玩具”项目，但其可用性已经通过日常使用得到了验证。他们对学习曲线、类Org模式功能以及是否支持插件表示关注，并对借鉴Helix的颜色主题设计表示赞赏。
• [xlii] 提到了另一个类似编辑器Anvil Editor，强调其受ACME启发、开放源代码以及可组合性，并指出其通过REST API与外部工具交互的功能。
• [paddy_m] 对Vim家族的扩展性提出疑问，并以Emacs为例，说明其通过Lisp解释器实现扩展的方式，暗示对该项目扩展性的关注。
• [scuff3d] 对项目中的bug持宽容态度，表示有兴趣探索代码库。
• [imiric] 赞赏项目的同时，特别关注其未来的扩展性，并建议利用现有生态系统的插件以避免从零开始。
• [nickandbrock] 对项目的颜色主题表示赞赏，并提到自己的项目，表示可能会借鉴该项目的颜色设计。
• [lsllc] 对项目使用diff进行撤销/重做的设计表示赞赏。
• [wyclif] 以幽默的方式建议改名，未提出功能性意见。
• [hit8run] 表示支持并鼓励项目继续发展，提到自己目前使用Helix作为终端代码编辑器，并愿意尝试该新项目。
• [tempfile] 关注该项目与Vim的不同之处，询问其相比Vim更有效的功能特点。

补充讨论：
• 项目的扩展性是讨论的焦点之一，多位评论者（paddy_m, imiric）对此表示关注，并以Vim和Emacs为例进行比较。
• 颜色主题和用户界面设计得到了多位评论者的赞赏（GuiShou, nickandbrock）。
• 不同编辑器之间的比较和借鉴（如Helix和Anvil Editor）也是讨论的一个重要方面（GuiShou, xlii）。
• 项目的创新性设计（如使用diff进行撤销/重做）引起了积极的反响（lsllc）。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明显的争议，但扩展性问题是一个潜在的讨论热点，涉及到项目未来的发展方向和生态建设。

McWig (temporary name)
Hi! Welcome to my text editor page.
McWig is a modal, Vim-like text editor written in Go. I use it as my daily driver, btw.
Note:
McWig currently supports only
.go
files. Do not edit files that are not backed up. McWig is still in an early stage of development and may damage your files.
Features
LSP autocomplete, goto definition, hover info
Tree-sitter support
Color themes (borrowed from the Helix text editor)
Lots of bugs
Macro support
Something like Emacs org-mode: Open
test.txt
, place the cursor at line 15, and press
"Ctrl-C Ctrl-C"
.
This project was written as a "speed run" — not for speed in terms of time, but rather as an exercise to explore the text editor problem space without overthinking or planning ahead. It’s a quick and "dirty" implementation, so to speak.
Running
make setup-runtime
make build-run
Keybindings
Most common Vim keybindings are implemented, providing minimal but enough (for me) support for daily source code editing. See
config/config.go
for all implemented keybindings.
To get started:

data.title: A Dark Adtech Empire Fed by Fake CAPTCHAs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
2024年，安全研究人员发现克里姆林宫支持的虚假信息活动通过恶意广告技术绕过社交媒体审核，该技术还被用于推广在线诈骗和攻击网站。Qurium公司的调查揭示了一个名为“Doppelganger”的虚假信息网络，该网络通过克隆网站传播亲俄内容，并使用复杂的“域名伪装”技术躲避审查。Doppelganger与VexTrio共享基础设施，后者是已知最古老的恶意流量分发系统（TDS），常通过钓鱼和社交工程骗局引导流量。

Doppelganger的伪装服务通过瑞士网络提供商进行域名重定向，并与成人约会网站LosPollos和TacoLoco共享基础设施。LosPollos借用《绝命毒师》主题吸引会员，利用被黑客攻击的WordPress网站传播恶意链接。TacoLoco则通过欺骗性弹窗通知获利。

Qurium进一步发现，LosPollos和TacoLoco由捷克和俄罗斯注册的公司Adspro运营，其基础设施由瑞士供应商Teknology SA提供，并与Guilio Vitorrio Leonardo Cerutti有关。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络广告和流量变现网络中的欺骗性策略，尤其是通过浏览器推送通知进行的攻击，以及用户如何受到影响和应对方法。

不同观点：
• [LegionMammal978] 分享了亲身经历，一位老年亲属的电脑因误点击允许了浏览器推送通知，导致桌面被垃圾消息轰炸。他通过设置浏览器自动拒绝通知来防止再次发生。这表明普通用户，尤其是老年用户，容易受到此类攻击的影响。

• [psychoslave] 提到虽然流量分发系统（TDS）常被合法广告网络使用，但VexTrio的TDS主要通过网络钓鱼、恶意软件和社会工程骗局来管理流量。指出即使是非法活动者也常自认为其行为合法。

• [preinheimer] 认为“通过点击按钮证明你是人类”的攻击方式很巧妙，在当今各种验证方式中可能会欺骗很多用户。

• [justusthane] 和 [BMaronge] 都对用户在点击链接后被引导通过一系列域名再到达目标内容的行为表示疑惑，并询问这种操作的目的。

• [b0a04gl] 将浏览器推送通知视为新的弹出广告，认为它提供了不良用户体验，且用户未被明确询问是否接受此类通知。

• [thyristan] 深入分析了浏览器在处理网站权限请求时的混乱和不一致性，建议浏览器需要更一致和透明的权限管理界面，以防止用户被误导。

• [tempodox] 感叹在欺诈和盗窃行为中，创造力被极端利用。

• [HocusLocus] 分享了教导年长用户识别虚假系统对话的经验，并提到需要更多教育来防止用户被骗，同时提及俄罗斯网络活动对欧盟的潜在威胁。

• [tehwebguy] 对某个移动平台不允许浏览器推送通知表示感激。

• [username223] 质疑为何恶意代码（如JavaScript）能够发送操作系统级别的通知，认为浏览器应限制代码执行环境，防止网络攻击面的扩大。

• [StuntPope] 对文章中涉及“克里姆林宫虚假信息”的内容持怀疑态度，批评Krebs的文章有时存在误导性。

• [wwn_se] 推荐使用Adblock作为解决方案，认为通过广告拦截可以有效保护用户免受恶意广告影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Krebs文章中提及的“克里姆林宫虚假信息”，部分用户对其真实性和文章的客观性提出质疑。
• 另一个讨论点是浏览器在处理推送通知和其他权限请求时的用户界面设计问题，用户认为需要更透明和一致的权限管理。
• 关于TacoLoco网络的欺骗性策略，用户普遍认为需要更多用户教育和技术解决方案来防止此类攻击。

44263780.article_content:
Late last year, security researchers made a startling discovery: Kremlin-backed disinformation campaigns were bypassing moderation on social media platforms by leveraging the same malicious advertising technology that powers a sprawling ecosystem of online hucksters and website hackers. A new report on the fallout from that investigation finds this dark ad tech industry is far more resilient and incestuous than previously known.
Image: Infoblox.
In November 2024, researchers at the security firm
Qurium
published an investigation into “
Doppelganger
,” a disinformation network that promotes pro-Russian narratives and infiltrates Europe’s media landscape by pushing fake news through a network of cloned websites.
Doppelganger campaigns use specialized links that bounce the visitor’s browser through a long series of domains before the fake news content is served. Qurium
found
Doppelganger relies on a sophisticated “domain cloaking” service, a technology that allows websites to present different content to search engines compared to what regular visitors see. The use of cloaking services helps the disinformation sites remain online longer than they otherwise would, while ensuring that only the targeted audience gets to view the intended content.
Qurium discovered that Doppelganger’s cloaking service also promoted online dating sites, and shared much of the same infrastructure with
VexTrio
, which is thought to be the oldest malicious traffic distribution system (TDS) in existence. While TDSs are commonly used by legitimate advertising networks to manage traffic from disparate sources and to track who or what is behind each click, VexTrio’s TDS largely manages web traffic from victims of phishing, malware, and social engineering scams.
BREAKING BAD
Digging deeper, Qurium noticed Doppelganger’s cloaking service used an Internet provider in Switzerland as the first entry point in a chain of domain redirections. They also noticed the same infrastructure hosted a pair of co-branded affiliate marketing services that were driving traffic to sketchy adult dating sites:
LosPollos[.]com
and
TacoLoco[.]co
.
The LosPollos ad network incorporates many elements and references from the hit series “Breaking Bad,” mirroring the fictional “Los Pollos Hermanos” restaurant chain that served as a money laundering operation for a violent methamphetamine cartel.
The LosPollos advertising network invokes characters and themes from the hit show Breaking Bad. The logo for LosPollos (upper left) is the image of Gustavo Fring, the fictional chicken restaurant chain owner in the show.
Affiliates who sign up with LosPollos are given JavaScript-heavy “
smartlinks
” that drive traffic into the VexTrio TDS, which in turn distributes the traffic among a variety of advertising partners, including dating services, sweepstakes offers, bait-and-switch mobile apps, financial scams and malware download sites.
LosPollos affiliates typically stitch these smart links into
WordPress
websites that have been hacked via known vulnerabilities, and those affiliates will earn a small commission each time an Internet user referred by any of their hacked sites falls for one of these lures.
The Los Pollos advertising network promoting itself on LinkedIn.
According to Qurium, TacoLoco is a traffic monetization network that uses deceptive tactics to trick Internet users into enabling “push notifications,” a
cross-platform browser standard
that allows websites to show pop-up messages which appear outside of the browser. For example, on Microsoft Windows systems these notifications typically show up in the bottom right corner of the screen — just above the system clock.
In the case of VexTrio and TacoLoco, the notification approval requests themselves are deceptive — disguised as “CAPTCHA” challenges designed to distinguish automated bot traffic from real visitors. For years, VexTrio and its partners have successfully tricked countless users into enabling these site notifications, which are then used to continuously pepper the victim’s device with a variety of phony virus alerts and misleading pop-up messages.
Examples of VexTrio landing pages that lead users to accept push notifications on their device.
According to
a December 2024 annual report
from
GoDaddy
,
nearly 40 percent of compromised websites in 2024 redirected visitors to VexTrio via LosPollos smartlinks
.
ADSPRO AND TEKNOLOGY
On November 14, 2024, Qurium

2024年，安全研究人员发现克里姆林宫支持的虚假信息活动通过恶意广告技术绕过社交媒体审核，该技术还被用于推广在线诈骗和攻击网站。Qurium公司的调查揭示了一个名为“Doppelganger”的虚假信息网络，该网络通过克隆网站传播亲俄内容，并使用复杂的“域名伪装”技术躲避审查。Doppelganger与VexTrio共享基础设施，后者是已知最古老的恶意流量分发系统（TDS），常通过钓鱼和社交工程骗局引导流量。

Doppelganger的伪装服务通过瑞士网络提供商进行域名重定向，并与成人约会网站LosPollos和TacoLoco共享基础设施。LosPollos借用《绝命毒师》主题吸引会员，利用被黑客攻击的WordPress网站传播恶意链接。TacoLoco则通过欺骗性弹窗通知获利。

Qurium进一步发现，LosPollos和TacoLoco由捷克和俄罗斯注册的公司Adspro运营，其基础设施由瑞士供应商Teknology SA提供，并与Guilio Vitorrio Leonardo Cerutti有关。

The Case for Software Craftsmanship in the Era of Vibes
They tell me software developers will soon be replaced by autonomous agents.
Yet every single day, I encounter bad software.
When AGI comes, can its first assignment be to ship a decent calendar app?
I'm not here to complain about bad software, at least not in this post.
I'm here to make the case for quality software in an era where constraints on code production have been dramatically lifted.
When Limits Disappear, Quality Should Matter More
You can vibe code at a
buttery-smooth 120fps in Zed
and generate code 24 hours a day if you're so inclined.
But in a world of abundance, the bar should be higher for quality.
As software engineers, we should measure our contribution not in lines of code generated, but in reliable, well-designed systems that are easy to change and a pleasure to use.
There's a lot of talk online about the 10x (or even the 100x!) engineer.
Most people are talking about how AI can help us make software faster and help us make more software.
As craftspeople, we should look at AI and ask, "How can this help me build better software?"
System Design Matters More
If you've spent any time in a codebase that solves real problems, I'm sure you can relate to this sentiment: "I want this to be better, but I don't have time to fix it."
The system is broken in ways that hobble our productivity and imagination, but we need to ship.
There's always an incentive to achieve our goals by bending the existing system instead of revising it, even if that leaves the system "not quite right, but good enough."
Our
values at Zed
of "Shipping & Craftsmanship" exist as a pair for a reason.
We should feel urgency, but we shouldn't be using urgency as an excuse to cut corners.
Short-term gains aren't worth the cost of suboptimal velocity for the lifetime of the company.
This is even more true now that a gnarly code base hinders not only our own ability to work in it, but also the ability of AI tools to be effective in it.
Recognizing this dynamic doesn't make it any easier to resolve.
Since we're only learning about a system as we build it, we may not even know what the "right design" is until rather far into the system's development.
Each of our many decisions may make sense in the moment, but over time they accumulate, and before we know it we find ourselves working in what feels like a legacy codebase—despite trying at every turn to avoid that outcome.
All of this makes it more critical than ever to evaluate contributions not by how many lines of code you touched, but by your impact on how reliable, understandable, and changeable the resulting system will be.
Taking Ownership and Raising the Bar
So how do we build good software? There are probably multiple ways, but I'll tell you mine.
It requires taking ownership of the user's experience.
As a user of a code editor, I want a fast experience.
If complex 3D games can run at 120 frames per second, there's no reason my editor couldn't render 2D text and rectangles that fast.
That was my initial goal for Zed, although at the time I didn't know how to achieve it.
One thing I did know, based on my past experience creating a
code editor named Atom
(and
its spinoff, Electron
), is that I'd have to look beyond web technology.
Otherwise, I'd never be able to achieve an experience better than a web browser.
So I started over.
But starting over meant taking on a much wider scope, learning a systems programming language with a sadistically helpful compiler, and learning to write shaders.
All of that added risk to the project, but without it, Zed couldn't have become what it is today.
Luckily, that kind of learning and de novo software development just got vastly easier, thanks to the power of LLMs.
Even with hallucinations, I would have given almost anything to have a language model chat me through Rust borrow checker errors when I was first learning.
Taking full ownership over the user's experience is not as risky as it used to be.
If we have the ambition to pursue an amazing experience, but only some of the skills necessary to deliver it, AI can help us overcome the knowledge gaps standing in our way.
It won't be a drop-in substitute for actual expertise, and we'll still make mistakes as we go, but it will let us experiment faster, learn faster, and iterate faster than we ever could in the old days.
Aim high! The barrier to entry to building truly great experiences has never been lower.
Let's Figure It Out Together
AI agents have not existed for very long.
We've already learned a lot about how best to use them, but there remains much to learn.
What's more, the tools themselves continue to improve, which creates ever-moving goalposts in our pursuit of understanding.
In this rapidly evolving environment, how can we determine which skills and techniques work best with which tools?
The same way we always have: sharing knowledge with one another!
That's why today, we're
introducing Agentic Engineering
—combinin

data.title: The Sixties Come Back to Life in "Everything Is Now"
data.author: tintinnabula
data.article_summary: J. Hoberman的《Everything Is Now: The 1960s New York Avant-Garde》深入探讨了1960年代纽约前卫艺术的蓬勃发展，包括原始表演、地下电影和激进流行文化。本书信息密集，融合了新闻调查、深刻分析和敏锐的批评判断，以独特的档案式热情呈现。Hoberman通过个人参与和大量研究，重现了那个时代的艺术活力和重要声音，特别关注媒体与艺术的相互作用以及本地政治与文化生活的交织。书中频繁提及警察和逮捕，反映了法律对前卫艺术的压制，展现了前卫艺术与法律的冲突。通过描述诸如Beat文学、Amiri Baraka和Lenny Bruce等案例，Hoberman揭示了前卫艺术在反抗与压制中的发展，使本书不仅是一部文化史，也是一部政治史。

主要讨论点：评论围绕不同时间和地点的文化创意场景及其成因展开，特别关注低租金对艺术和音乐场景的影响，同时涉及到历史事件对文化的影响以及代际文化差异的争议。

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun认为低租金是推动城市创意活力的关键因素。他通过举例说明，例如80年代乔治亚州雅典的“大学音乐”场景以及堪萨斯城的艺术学院周边社区，都因低租金吸引了创意人群和文化活动。他还通过个人经历描述了这些社区中的独特艺术景观。

• rurban则将讨论引向电影历史中的理论对立，提到Hoberman支持的自毁理论，并以Cimino的《天堂之门》失败为例。同时，他提到Tarantino对曼森谋杀案中猎巫行动的反对理论，质疑这些历史事件对现今文化的影响。rurban还暗示了对“取消文化”的批评，认为这是一种过度行为。

• Telemakhos对持续复兴的60年代文化表示不满，认为这是婴儿潮一代对过去时代的怀旧情结，并抱怨自己随着年龄增长而感受到的代际不平衡。

补充讨论：
• JKCalhoun的评论中提到了具体的艺术和音乐场景，强调了低租金对创意社区形成的重要性。
• rurban的评论引发了关于历史事件和文化变迁的深层次思考，特别是对“取消文化”的批评，暗示了当代文化中的一些争议。
• Telemakhos的观点揭示了代际之间的文化差异和对过去时代的不同态度，指出了持续怀旧现象的潜在不满。

争议焦点：
• 低租金是否是推动创意场景形成的最重要因素。
• 历史事件如曼森谋杀案对文化的影响及其在现代的延续性。
• 代际文化差异以及对60年代文化持续复兴的不满。

这些观点展示了不同角度对文化和历史影响的复杂理解，同时揭示了代际之间的文化冲突和价值观差异。

The film critic and cultural historian J. Hoberman’s new book, “
Everything Is Now: The 1960s New York Avant-Garde—Primal Happenings, Underground Movies, Radical Pop
,” is as jubilantly overstuffed as its subtitle. The book is a startlingly slow read—and I say that with unbridled enthusiasm. I can’t remember the last book I’ve read that contained so much information so tightly packed, or in which the distillation of vast research offered such relentless ricochets of association, connection, and allusion. Although its meld of journalistic detective work, insightful analysis, and keen critical judgment might suggest a straightforward nonfiction account, it’s a work of obsession and devotion that finds a distinctive and original form—a hectic informational voracity—for its passionate archivism.
Hoberman, who was born in 1949, grew up in Queens, and frequented Manhattan’s downtown scene as a teen-ager and young adult. In the course of his narrative, he sometimes revisits, as a historian, events that he attended and even one in which he had a hand. The last line of “Everything Is Now”—forgive my spoiler—in which he refers to “this book, which I consider a memoir, although not mine,” is a keenly self-conscious, poetic, and philosophical encapsulation of the paradoxically personal yet impersonal ambition energizing the project. The ideal of collective memory is built into the very nature of Hoberman’s research. A film critic for the
Village Voice
from 1978 to 2012, he is up-front about the major role that this long-crucial weekly and other downtown publications played in his investigations: “To write this book, I not only interviewed witnesses and participants but read through virtually every copy of the
Voice
between late 1958 and early 1972, along with much of the
East Village Other
,
Rat
, and the New York
Free Press
.” The result is something of a citational history, bringing to life the wild artistic ferment of the times, along with many of the era’s vital voices.
The cover of J. Hoberman's new book, “Everything Is Now: The 1960s New York Avant-Garde—Primal Happenings, Underground Movies, Radical Pop.”
The characters who inhabit “Everything Is Now” make for an extraordinary cast. After reading the book, it’s as if one had been all over town all decade long, with a dazzling array of companions, and readers are likely to come away from the kaleidoscopic whirl with their own highlights and affinities. The book suggests that what had burst through earlier generations’ veils of decorum in this period was personality, the drive to be oneself in public—or, alternatively, to create a public persona in one’s own self-determined image. Hoberman identifies the downtown of the nineteen-sixties as a world of media: the art scene that emerged was inextricable both from the way that media depicted and amplified it and from the ability of artists and other figures to draw media attention. He chronicles a performative decade in which image confronted reality, converged with reality, became an inseparable part of reality, but still didn’t control it—because metaphors of power weren’t power and images of power weren’t power. Thus “Everything Is Now” is also a political history.
Hoberman’s account tracks how the city’s cultural life was intertwined with leftist politics and such activities as protest, disruption, and even destruction. Hoberman pays due attention to the major national and international events that influenced New York’s avant-garde—civil rights, the Vietnam War, political assassinations—and also to historic doings within the city, such as feminist activism and the Stonewall uprising. But he places particular emphasis on power at the local level and, most of all, on its prime physical manifestation: policing.
Search in the book for the words “police” (more than a hundred mentions) and “arrest” (more than fifty) to get a synoptic measure of the force of law opposing the New York avant-garde. Early on, Hoberman shows the literature of the Beats giving rise to performance, both in film (“Pull My Daisy”) and, crucially, live, in cafés. Because many of these were underground literally (basements) and figuratively (unlicensed), this led to legal trouble, in the form of summonses and inspections. As the art of the avant-garde became more audacious, the law intervened more intensely. Many of the arrests were for obscenity: in 1961, Amiri Baraka (then called LeRoi Jones) was arrested at his home, on Fourteenth Street, for mailing the magazine
The Floating Bear
, of which he was co-editor; Lenny Bruce, famously, was arrested in 1964 for “indecent performance”; in 1968, a humble newspaper vender in Brooklyn was arrested for selling an underground comic.
Similarly, the charge of obscenity led to Shirley Clarke’s 1961 film, “
The Connection
,” being denied a license, a prerequisite for commercial release; when it was screened anyway, the projectionist was arrested.
44219822.article_summary: J. Hoberman的《Everything Is Now: The 1960s New York Avant-Garde》深入探讨了1960年代纽约前卫艺术的蓬勃发展，包括原始表演、地下电影和激进流行文化。本书信息密集，融合了新闻调查、深刻分析和敏锐的批评判断，以独特的档案式热情呈现。Hoberman通过个人参与和大量研究，重现了那个时代的艺术活力和重要声音，特别关注媒体与艺术的相互作用以及本地政治与文化生活的交织。书中频繁提及警察和逮捕，反映了法律对前卫艺术的压制，展现了前卫艺术与法律的冲突。通过描述诸如Beat文学、Amiri Baraka和Lenny Bruce等案例，Hoberman揭示了前卫艺术在反抗与压制中的发展，使本书不仅是一部文化史，也是一部政治史。
44219822.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕不同时间和地点的文化创意场景及其成因展开，特别关注低租金对艺术和音乐场景的影响，同时涉及到历史事件对文化的影响以及代际文化差异的争议。

不同观点：

• rurban则将讨论引向电影历史中的理论对立，提到Hoberman支持的自毁理论，并以Cimino的《天堂之门》失败为例。同时，他提到Tarantino对曼森谋杀案中猎巫行动的反对理论，质疑这些历史事件对现今文化的影响。rurban还暗示了对“取消文化”的批评，认为这是一种过度行为。

• Telemakhos对持续复兴的60年代文化表示不满，认为这是婴儿潮一代对过去时代的怀旧情结，并抱怨自己随着年龄增长而感受到的代际不平衡。

补充讨论：
• JKCalhoun的评论中提到了具体的艺术和音乐场景，强调了低租金对创意社区形成的重要性。
• rurban的评论引发了关于历史事件和文化变迁的深层次思考，特别是对“取消文化”的批评，暗示了当代文化中的一些争议。
• Telemakhos的观点揭示了代际之间的文化差异和对过去时代的不同态度，指出了持续怀旧现象的潜在不满。

争议焦点：
• 低租金是否是推动创意场景形成的最重要因素。
• 历史事件如曼森谋杀案对文化的影响及其在现代的延续性。
• 代际文化差异以及对60年代文化持续复兴的不满。

这些观点展示了不同角度对文化和历史影响的复杂理解，同时揭示了代际之间的文化冲突和价值观差异。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了网站为了防止AI公司大规模抓取数据导致的服务器过载，采用了名为Anubis的保护系统。Anubis使用了一种类似于Hashcash的“工作量证明”机制，增加大规模抓取的成本，同时尽量不影响普通用户。其目的是在开发更精准的识别技术之前，提供一个临时的解决方案。用户需要启用现代JavaScript功能，某些插件可能需要禁用才能正常访问网站。当前网站使用的Anubis版本是1.19.1。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语法高亮的实用性及其局限性，特别是在Vim等编辑器中的实现方式，以及可能的替代方案或改进方向。

不同观点：
• norir认为语法高亮常常让人分心，并且在解决问题时没有实际帮助。他更希望获得关于代码正确性的直接反馈，而不是仅仅依赖语法高亮。他主张手动高亮，并建议开发更智能、更快速的编译器来直接响应代码问题。
• chrismorgan承认粗略解析在基础编程语言中的作用，但指出其在语义细节上的不足。他提到Vim等编辑器的语法高亮存在局限性，特别是在处理函数定义和调用时，且在处理某些语言如C时尤其明显。他还提到，Vim的语法高亮有时会导致编辑速度变慢，需要更好的工具来识别问题所在。
• frou_dh支持完全准确的语法高亮，认为不准确的高亮（假阳性和假阴性）会对用户产生负面影响。他强调了准确高亮的优点，并暗示这是提升编辑器体验的重要因素。
• b0a04gl指出Vim的语法引擎缺乏对上下文的跟踪，无法处理如ysh语言中命令和表达模式混合的情况。他主张停止在Vim中叠加各种技巧，建议在外部生成语义标记，让Vim只负责渲染。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Vim语法高亮的具体技术限制，特别是其在处理复杂语言结构时的不足。
• 有人提到Oils等新语言通过明确的关键字（如`proc`）来简化语法高亮，这表明语言设计本身也可能影响高亮的效果。
• 讨论还涉及到对更智能工具和编译器的需求，这些工具可以提供更直接的代码反馈，而不仅仅是通过语法高亮。

争议焦点：语法高亮是否有助于编程效率，还是反而会成为一种视觉干扰。另外，Vim的语法高亮机制是否足够高效和准确，是否需要外部工具的辅助。

44265216.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
Why am I seeing this?
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up
Anubis
to protect the server against the scourge of
AI companies aggressively scraping websites
. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a
Proof-of-Work
scheme in the vein of
Hashcash
, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a hack whose real purpose is to give a "good enough" placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like
JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.
This website is running Anubis version
1.19.1
.

data.title: WebKit Standards Positions
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了如何查看WebKit在各类标准上的立场。用户需要启用JavaScript以访问交互式的标准立场总结表。如果无法启用JavaScript，文章建议直接浏览GitHub上的standards-positions代码库以获取相关信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Webkit团队在隐私、安全与web功能改进之间的决策感到矛盾，并讨论了其他浏览器如Mozilla的标准立场。

不同观点：
• [afavour的观点]
  ◦ 支持Webkit团队对隐私和安全的严格标准，但同时认为他们在某些决策上过于保守，可能以隐私和安全为借口限制了web平台的发展。
  ◦ 举例：Webkit反对在Progressive Web App（PWA）的manifest中添加截图，理由是截图可能被恶意使用，伪装成原生UI。
  ◦ 质疑：虽然截图可能被滥用，但网页上的任何图片都可能存在相同问题，因此质疑Webkit的反对是否合理，还是为了抵制App Store的替代方案。
  ◦ 补充：指出Safari甚至不支持这些安装提示，因此该反对立场的影响有限。

• [bsmth的观点]
  ◦ 对帖子内容表示兴趣，并提供Mozilla类似的标准立场链接，供其他用户参考和查阅。
  ◦ 提供链接：https://mozilla.github.io/standards-positions/

• [jazzypants的观点]
  ◦ 希望Webkit团队能直接链接至具体立场声明，以便更清晰地了解他们反对某些看似合理功能（如JSON应用manifest）的原因。
  ◦ 表达了对透明度和详细解释的需求。

补充讨论：
• Webkit团队在隐私和安全方面的严格标准获得了一定支持，但也引发了是否过度限制web功能改进的争议。
• 用户对Webkit反对某些功能的具体理由表示关注，并希望获得更详细的解释和透明度。
• 提到了其他浏览器（如Mozilla）的标准立场，提供了更多参考资料。

争议焦点：
• Webkit是否以隐私和安全为借口，限制了web平台的功能改进，特别是与App Store替代方案相关的功能。
• 用户对Webkit反对某些功能的具体理由缺乏详细了解，希望获得更透明的解释。

• Noelia- 认为网页设计初看有些 awkward，但随着时间推移，这种节奏变得合适。她指出这种设计让读者放慢速度，对于这首诗来说是有效的，虽然不会立刻吸引人，但若耐心阅读几分钟，会逐渐产生共鸣。

• b0a04gl 引用诗中的一段，解读其深层含义，认为诗中表达的是一种深层次的无力感，即人们不仅无法赢得改变，甚至不认为自己有机会参与其中，这种心态非常深刻。

• jihadjihad 提供了诗歌的原始文本链接，指出这首诗创作于1994年，将讨论引向诗歌本身的创作时间。

• zem 对诗中的特定词汇 "shell-y skylark" 表示赞赏，认为其使用非常巧妙。

• dash2 提供了另一首关于弱小缓慢生物的诗歌链接，并指出其中含有战争的暗示，试图引导讨论向其他相关诗歌扩展。

• tptacek 提出一个质疑，询问为什么特别选择这首诗进行讨论，表现出对选择这首诗的原因感兴趣。

• darepublic 引用诗中的一句话 "Patience, the sport of truly chastened things" 作为回应，似乎以此表达对诗歌主题的理解或共鸣。

• neonate 提供了一个存档链接，但没有进一步的解释或讨论。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了诗歌的深层解读，特别是对诗中表达的无助感和心理状态的分析（b0a04gl）。
• 部分用户分享了相关诗歌链接（dash2）和原始文本链接（jihadjihad），扩展了讨论的范围。
• 用户对网页设计的体验分享（Noelia-）引发了对这种设计选择是否有效的思考。
• 存在对诗歌选择原因的质疑（tptacek），表明讨论中有人对背景或动机感兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点可能在于为什么特别选择这首诗进行讨论（tptacek 的提问），以及这种网页设计是否真正有效，尽管 Noelia- 认为最终有效，但初看时感到 awkward。

data.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting: Our Search for a Time-Series Foundation Model
data.author: tiwarinitish86
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了时间序列预测领域从传统统计方法（如ARIMA、SARIMA、Prophet）向“基础模型”的转变，这些新模型借鉴了大型语言模型（LLMs）的零样本和迁移学习能力，旨在解决多样化时间序列数据的预测问题。文章介绍了对几种新兴的时间序列基础模型（如Amazon Chronos、Google TimesFM、IBM Tiny Time-Mixers、Datadog Toto）的评估，目标是测试这些模型在处理不同数据流时的表现，尤其是对摄入量预测和多变量指标预测的准确性。

文章详细描述了评估方法、数据预处理步骤、评估指标（如MAPE），以及模型在实际场景中的表现。研究发现，基础模型在处理多样化数据流和复杂场景时展现了较强的适应性和效率，能够减少对每个数据流单独调参和训练的需求，从而提升了可扩展性和预测质量。然而，模型仍面临一些现实挑战，如对异常数据的鲁棒性和跨领域应用的稳定性。总体而言，基础模型为时间序列预测带来了新的可能性，但仍需进一步优化以应对复杂多变的实际环境。

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby：认为时间序列基础模型的概念存在缺陷。他指出，基础模型应能够完成超出其训练目标的任务，而文章中提到的模型只是解决了无需重新训练即可进行分布外预测的问题。他还提到，现有的ARIMA和Prophet模型已经很好地解决了这一问题，且所需的计算资源和超参数选择都相对较少。此外，他认为探讨LLM架构是否能提升单变量或多变量时间序列预测的准确性更有意义。

Introduction
In the last few years, the field of time-series forecasting has seen a fundamental shift. Where we once depended solely on classic statistical methods, think
ARIMA
,
SARIMA
, and
Prophet
, new “foundation” models have emerged, promising to bring the power and flexibility of large language models (LLMs) into the world of time-series data. The allure is obvious: can we build a single, reusable forecasting model that works across a variety of datasets and domains, instead of painstakingly training a new model for every scenario?
Parseable
is built to handle our users’ observability data at any scale, a nonstop stream of raw ingest counts, infrastructure vitals, and fine-grained application signals. Running a separate, hand-tuned forecasting model for every slice quickly turns into a treadmill: each new stream or workload tweak demands fresh hyper-params, retrains, and ever-growing config sprawl. All that manual churn slows forecasts and breeds drift, so the results never feel fully trustworthy.
Then came the rise of foundation models, which revolutionised natural language processing by offering strong zero-shot and transfer learning capabilities. Researchers began asking a natural question: if LLMs can generalise to new tasks with minimal retraining, could similar techniques be applied to time-series data? What if you could just hand any telemetry stream to a pre-trained foundation model and immediately get a high-quality forecast, regardless of whether the model had seen data from that source before?
Motivated by this possibility, we set out to benchmark a new generation of time-series foundation models,
Amazon Chronos
,
Google TimesFM
,
IBM Tiny Time-Mixers
, and
Datadog Toto
.
Our goal was to assess how well these models perform on two representative tasks: a relatively straightforward forecasting problem (predicting ingestion volumes) and a more complex multivariate problem (forecasting multiple pod-level metrics). Along the way, we compared them to classical baselines and took note of both practical and technical trade-offs.
This post details our methodology, the challenges we encountered, how we evaluated the models, and what we learned from putting foundation models to the test on real-world observability data.
Why Foundation Models?
The idea of “foundation models” has fundamentally changed how we approach complex machine learning problems. In natural language processing, models like GPT have shown that a single, large model trained on vast and diverse datasets can generalize well to entirely new tasks sometimes even without fine-tuning. This zero-shot capability means a single model can perform sentiment analysis, summarization, translation, or question-answering, just by changing the prompt.
In the world of time-series forecasting, the appeal of such flexibility is obvious, especially for modern data engineering and observability platforms. Traditionally, every new data stream whether it’s CPU utilization, request rates, or disk I/O required its own model, hyperparameter tuning, and regular retraining. For an SRE or platform engineer, this quickly becomes unmanageable as the number of streams explodes. If a pipeline ingests data from a hundred microservices, does every service metric really need its own hand-tuned ARIMA or Prophet model? The answer, up until recently, was “yes.”
Foundation models for time series are built to change that. The core motivation is scalability and adaptability: train a single, large model (often with billions of parameters) on a wide range of time-series datasets and let it learn the underlying “language” of temporal data. Once trained, this model should ideally handle a completely new telemetry stream, even if it has never seen data of that exact shape or domain before. In theory, you could input any new time series, whether it’s network packet counts, database query durations, or energy consumption readings and get a high-quality forecast without retraining.
This is a huge leap from traditional approaches. Classic statistical models like ARIMA or seasonal decomposition excel when you have clean, stationary data and a well-understood seasonal pattern, but fall short when faced with missing values, sudden regime changes, or non-standard periodicity. More importantly, these models can’t transfer knowledge from one dataset to another; every dataset is a blank slate.

data.title: Show HN: I wrote a BitTorrent Client from scratch
data.author: piyushgupta53
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个用Go语言实现的BitTorrent客户端——go-torrent-client。该项目实现了BitTorrent客户端的核心功能，包括种子文件解析、节点发现与通信以及文件下载。主要特性包括Bencode编码/解码、种子文件处理、节点发现与通信、以及下载管理（如分片和块管理、进度跟踪等）。项目结构清晰，包含命令行界面、内部包（如Bencode编码、种子处理、节点协议等）以及公共包。目前该项目正在积极开发中，未来计划支持磁力链接、元数据交换协议和DHT。需要Go 1.21或更高版本进行安装和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言实现的BitTorrent客户端的实现细节、安全性、功能完整性及潜在改进方向

不同观点：
• [jorkingit] 认为需要限制bencode解码器中的动态分配大小，以防止恶意输入通过请求极大的分配来导致拒绝服务（DoS）攻击。建议将剩余的输入长度作为上限。
• [vkaku] 对项目表示赞赏，并建议在README中添加简单的使用说明，例如如何通过命令行下载.torrent文件。此外，还建议添加从URL解析torrent文件的功能。
• [__jonas] 提到一个名为codecrafters的平台，该平台提供相关课程并包含测试，可以作为实现BitTorrent客户端的指导。
• [ashirviskas] 作为一个非Go开发者，询问为什么使用较旧的Go版本1.21，并指出该版本已在10个月前被弃用。
• [agiron123] 表示该项目让他们回想起大学时的网络课程项目，并认为这种项目是学习新语言的好方法。
• [vivzkestrel] 对项目的构建过程表示好奇，询问作者是参考了协议文档还是通过其他实现来构建项目。

补充讨论：
• [NooneAtAll3] 询问是否支持磁力链接，并在编辑中提到这似乎是一个计划中的功能。
• [TheEdonian] 询问为该项目添加图形用户界面（GUI）的难度，并表示对Go语言的GUI实现不熟悉。
• [throwaway894345] 对项目的完整性和处理复杂功能（如DHT、磁力链接、NAT traversal）的能力表示关注，并询问项目的完成度和实现难度。
• [NoMoreNicksLeft] 询问是否实现了v2和可变torrent，并表示对可变torrent的支持非常重要。
• [OccamsMirror] 询问该项目是否可以作为库使用。
• [b0a04gl] 认为项目在崩溃恢复、加密握手、uTP支持和NAT行为等方面缺乏说明，并指出在真实环境中可能存在风险。建议增加模块化设计和内存保护机制，并提到需要一个roadmap。

争议焦点：
• 项目的安全性和功能完整性是主要争议点。一些评论者关注项目在处理恶意输入、复杂BitTorrent功能（如DHT、磁力链接）、以及在真实环境中的稳定性方面的能力。
• 另外，使用较旧的Go版本也引起了一些讨论。

Go-Torrent
A BitTorrent client implementation in Go that supports downloading files using the BitTorrent protocol. This project implements the core functionality of a BitTorrent client, including torrent file parsing, peer discovery, and file downloading.
Features
Bencode Encoding/Decoding
Support for all Bencode types (strings, integers, lists, dictionaries)
Robust error handling and validation
Torrent File Processing
Parse .torrent files (both single-file and multi-file torrents)
Info hash calculation
Piece hash extraction
Support for all standard torrent file fields
Peer Discovery and Communication
HTTP tracker support
Peer handshake protocol
Complete BitTorrent message protocol
Peer connection management
Download Functionality
Piece and block management
Concurrent downloads
Progress tracking
File assembly for both single and multi-file torrents
Storage management with block-level granularity
Project Structure
.
├── cmd/          # Command-line interface and main application
├── internal/     # Internal packages
│   ├── bencode/  # Bencode encoding/decoding
│   ├── torrent/  # Torrent file processing
│   ├── tracker/  # Tracker protocol implementation
│   ├── peer/     # Peer communication
│   └── download/ # Download management
└── pkg/          # Public packages

Go 1.21 or later

git clone https://github.com/yourusername/go-torrent.git
cd

go mod download

data.author: Ezpie
data.article_summary:
《忘记运行代码检查工具的艺术》（2025）——一位 wise old programmer

你是否曾在提交代码到生产环境前忘记运行代码检查工具（linter）？现在不用担心了！GetHooky 可以确保你再也不会犯这样的错误。它能在你进行代码提交或推送时自动测试和检查代码。

为什么选择 GetHooky？
1. 大多数 Git hook 工具仅支持特定编程语言或需要复杂配置，而 GetHooky 只需一次安装，即可跨平台、跨语言使用，且为命令行工具。
2. 支持所有 Git hooks，易于使用。

尽管在 Windows 上可能有些问题，但整体上 GetHooky 是一款便捷的工具，帮助开发者自动管理代码质量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕工具安装、使用以及与Git hooks关系的讨论

不同观点：
• G1N：尝试在macOS arm架构上通过rosetta安装工具，但遇到权限问题。他手动安装了x86版本到个人目录下以绕过权限错误，并建议对于darwin客户端可以尝试安装到/usr/local/bin目录以避免权限问题。

• ericyd：表达了对Git hooks工具的不同偏好。他认为CI可以确保必要的检查，因此不需要在本地使用Git hooks。他还提到，运行额外的测试或构建命令来验证代码功能对他来说足够了，Git hooks反而可能拖慢常见操作，因此更倾向于不使用它们。他认为该工具相比Husky等项目级配置有所改进，因为它是个人配置，可以自行选择是否使用。

• nodesocket：对工具文档网站的主题设计表示赞赏，关注点主要在视觉设计上，而非工具功能本身。

• ericyd提供了对Git hooks工具的不同使用偏好，强调个人工作流和CI的替代方案，认为工具选择应根据个人需求决定。
• nodesocket的评论更多是关于外观设计，并未涉及功能性讨论。
• greatgib对安装方式的抱怨反映了部分开发者对现代工具安装流程的不满，特别是涉及权限和系统兼容性时。

data.title: Plants hear their pollinators, and produce sweet nectar in response
data.author: marojejian
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：植物是否能够“听”声音并对其做出反应，特别是对不同类型昆虫的声音做出区分性反应。

不同观点：
• thinkling和marojejian认为，植物能够通过声音区分有效授粉者与盗取花蜜的非授粉者，并根据不同声音调整花蜜的产量。thinkling还引用了《The Light Eaters》一书，提到植物具有其他感官能力，如花朵形状像天线收集声音振动。
• raffael_de提供了相关研究的链接，指出虽然研究显示植物对昆虫飞行声音有反应，但目前可能还没有经过同行评审的论文。他引用的研究表明，植物对不同飞行行为产生的声音有不同的反应。
• IshKebab对植物能“听”声音的说法持怀疑态度，认为在看到同行评审的文章之前不应轻信，指出人们往往喜欢“植物能听到声音”的故事。
• Huxley1表示惊讶，认为植物能感知声音是新奇的发现，并提出植物可能还有其他未被发现的感觉输入方式。
• lutusp持批评态度，认为将人类特质赋予植物是“拟人化”的表现，可能误导理解自然选择的无情感、无浪漫的进化过程。

补充讨论：
• srameshc对自然界中这种相互关联的系统表示惊叹，认为科学发现揭示了自然界中隐藏的联系。
• ingohelpinger以幽默的方式提出，如果植物能听到声音，那么对它们说话和播放音乐可能有帮助。
• altruios从伦理角度讨论了植物如果能够做出选择和表达偏好，人类是否有义务考虑这些偏好，并引申到对实验室培养肉的需求。
• 其他如ramijames和csours的评论主要是轻松的调侃，未深入讨论科学内容。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于植物是否真的能够“听”声音并做出区分性反应。支持者引用了研究和书籍，而怀疑者则要求看到更严谨的科学证据。
• 另一个争议点在于是否将人类特质过度赋予植物，即“拟人化”问题，这可能会影响对科学发现的客观理解。

总体而言，讨论围绕植物对声音的反应能力展开，涉及科学证据的可信度、对自然现象的惊奇以及对拟人化的批判性思考。

data.title: Show HN: Tattoy – a text-based terminal compositor
data.author: tombh
data.article_summary: Tattoy是一个为现代终端设计的文本 compositor，通过GPU渲染着色器并提供TTY滚动缓冲区的实时更新小地图。它基于纯文本，适用于任何支持真彩色的终端模拟器，利用UTF8半块字符（▀, ▄）实现图形效果。其主要功能包括自动调整文本对比度、运行背景命令（如音频可视化、视频背景、系统监控图表）、以及自定义插件支持。Tattoy兼容Shader Toy和Ghostty着色器，并且可以在正常终端状态和特效之间快速切换。此外，它还管理自己的滚动缓冲区，并提供滚动条功能，确保文本对比度易读。插件可以通过JSON协议进行开发，支持任意语言。

A Text-Based Compositor For Modern Terminals
Tattoy with a GPU-rendered shader and live-updating minimap of the TTY scrollback.
About
Tattoy can generally be thought of as a framework for adding eye-candy to your terminal. It is purely text-based so works in any terminal emulator that supports true colour. "Graphics" is rendered with UTF8 half-blocks (▀,▄). Whilst most of its effects are for getting you street credibility it also has more powerful features based around its awareness of terminal contents. For example it can detect and auto adjust text contrast whilst remaining faithful to the terminal's palette.
Tattoy works with your existing shell, theme and prompt, etc. It can always and immediately toggle between its effects and your normal terminal state, allowing for easy copy-pasting for example.
Shaders
Perhaps the fanciest feature of Tattoy is its ability to render GPU shaders. It is designed to be able to run most shaders from
Shader Toy
without any editing at all. It also supports
Ghostty shaders
out-of-the-box, though certain shaders that alter the position of text (such as CRT emulators) don't have a pronounced impact as text rendering is always left to the host terminal emulator.
Second Terminal In Background
You can run an arbitrary command that is rendered in the background of your normal terminal. Use-cases for this might be:
an audio visualiser
video background
system monitor graphs
The background terminal's opacity can be adjusted so it doesn't visual conflict too much with your actual terminal.
Scrollback Minimap
The minimap is a pixelised version of the contents of the scrollback, including the current contents of the screen. It live updates, even when using the so-called "alternate screen" for apps like `nvim`, `top`, `gitui`, etc.
Tattoy manages its own scrollback buffer (like say `tmux` does), and so can therefore also provide its own scrollbar.
Auto Text Contrast
Have you ever run `ls` in a directory only for certain file types to be completely illegible? This has long been an intractable problem caused by the limited colours of terminal palettes. CLI applications are only ever aware of palette index values, not the underlying RGB value, therefore it is impossible for them to know if any given background colour is sufficient enough to allow its containing text to be readable.
Not anymore!
Tattoy is aware of the true 24 bit RGBA value of all colours in your terminal. This allows it to use clever algorithms to detect low contrast text and auto adjust the foreground colour within the constraints of your chosen terminal theme to find the nearest colour that meets a minimum contrast threshold.
Plugins
Plugins can be written in any language. You get full access to your terminal's contents and can render both UTF8 "pixels" and text to a dedicated plugin layer of your choosing. Currently the protocol is JSON over `STDIN` and `STDOUT`. See the
plugin documentation
for more info.
Here we see the cursor giving off smoke particles that interact with the terminal's text. The source code can be found
here
.

• [hnlmorg] 认为Tattoy解决的低对比度文本问题早已有解决方案（高对比度终端主题），并指出更大的问题是使用8位或16位颜色ANSI码的软件会覆盖终端主题。他还提到有人不同意其对这种行为的“ rude”评价。
• [ramon156] 对Tattoy的定制化能力表示赞赏，称之为“term ricing的巅峰”。
• [pvg] 提供了项目的GitHub链接，为其他用户提供进一步了解和参与的途径。
• [TheSilva] 关注Tattoy对Windows系统的支持情况，质疑其在发布计划中的反复变化。

补充讨论：
• [em-bee] 提到Tattoy自行管理滚动缓冲区（类似`tmux`），并提出两个问题：是否所有GUI终端都这样做，以及在Tattoy中使用`tmux`会发生什么。此外，询问是否有浅色主题的示例。
• [d4rkp4ttern] 对“compositor”一词感到困惑，质疑一般技术人员是否应该知道其含义。
• [nerflad] 对项目表示赞赏，并送上良好祝愿。
• [otterpro] 表示可能会运行cmatrix或htop以增强视觉效果，并对项目截图中的“Rick-rolled”彩蛋表示兴趣。
• [msgodel] 认为项目更像是一个流媒体SVG渲染器而非VTE，并对此创意表示认可。
• [grandma_tea] 对Tattoy的插件和着色器交互可能性表示兴趣，提出是否可以实现终端中的火焰效果。
• [pacifika] 对项目的创新思维表示赞赏。
• [gfalcao] 简单直接地表达了对项目的极度赞赏。
• [MatthewPhillips] 对项目的出色表现表示赞赏和祝贺。

争议焦点：
• Tattoy所解决的问题是否真的是“新”问题（[tfsh]、[hnlmorg]）。
• 项目自动播放视频是否影响用户体验（[djaychela]）。
• 对“compositor”一词的理解差异（[d4rkp4ttern]）。

总体来看，评论多为正面评价，技术讨论集中在项目功能实现、错误调试及与其他工具的兼容性上。

data.title: 100 years of Zermelo's axiom of choice: What was the problem with it? (2006)
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了集合论中的良序原理和选择公理的历史发展。康托尔在1879-1884年间发表的系列论文中提出了每个集合都可以被良好排序的观点，但未能成功证明。1904年，策梅洛首次成功证明了良序原理，但前提是引入了选择公理。这一证明引发了数学界对选择公理的广泛讨论，策梅洛随后在1908年发表了第二篇论文，包含了对选择公理的新表述和良序定理的新证明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于拓扑学和集合论中选择公理（Axiom of Choice, AoC）及其变种、应用和直觉理解的讨论。

不同观点：
• **[math_comment_21]**: 提出在拓扑学中，连续满射映射不一定具有连续分裂映射（即每个满射都可以分裂为某种“部分逆”）。例如，从单位区间到圆的映射无法连续分裂，而集合论中的选择公理则保证了集合范畴中的每个满射都可以分裂。这种对比显示了不同数学范畴下选择公理的适用性差异。作者还提到，可以根据需求选择不同的范畴进行研究，例如不使用选择公理定义新的代数结构。

• **[mietek]**: 强调了直觉主义数学和类型论的历史材料的机械化（即将数学理论形式化并用计算机验证）。他邀请其他人推荐一些不太为人知的材料，以便让更多人了解这些内容。

• **[jfengel]**: 指出选择公理的构造性版本是“显然正确的”，但与经典的Zermelo选择公理不同，后者会导致不想要的结果（如排中律）。他还询问了目前学术界对这些结果的共识以及是否有任何显著的改进。

• **[jasperry]**: 试图澄清选择公理的构造性版本与经典版本之间的区别，强调Zermelo的选择公理在构造性数学中会导致不期望的结果（如排中律），并询问当前是否已有共识和重要进展。

• **[CliffStoll]**: 通过引用Banach-Tarski悖论来说明选择公理的反直觉性质，强调了选择公理的一些极端结果（如将一个豌豆分解并重组成一个太阳），这些结果与日常直觉相悖。

• **[scoofy]**: 认为公理是任意的，关键在于它们是否有用，强调了选择公理的实用性而非其内在的真理。

• **[impostervt]**: 表示对选择公理的理解有困难，请求用简单的语言解释（ELI5）。

• **[munificent]**: 虽然对讨论内容不太理解，但对页面的设计和排版表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是选择公理在不同数学范畴中的适用性及其直觉上的反常结果。例如，Banach-Tarski悖论展示了选择公理在集合论中的反直觉应用。
• 另一个讨论点是选择公理的构造性版本与经典版本的区别，以及它们在不同数学框架下的影响和应用。
• 讨论还涉及到对数学公理系统的选择自由，即研究者可以根据具体需求选择不同的公理系统和范畴进行研究。

Cantor conceived set theory in a sequence of six papers published in the
Mathematische Annalen
during the five year period 1879–1884. In the fifth of these papers, published in 1883,
1
he stated as a law of thought (
Denkgesetz
) that every set can be well-ordered or, more precisely, that it is always possible to bring any well-defined set into the form of a well-ordered set. Now to call it a law of thought was implicitly to claim self-evidence for it, but he must have given up that claim at some point, because in the 1890s he made an unsuccessful attempt at demonstrating the well-ordering principle.
2
The first to succeed in doing so was Zermelo,
3
although, as a prerequisite of the demonstration, he had to introduce a new principle, which came to be called the principle of choice (
Prinzip der Auswahl
) respectively the axiom of choice (
Axiom der Auswahl
) in his two
4
papers
5
from 1908. His first paper on the subject, published in 1904, consists of merely three pages, excerpted by Hilbert from a letter which he had received from Zermelo. The letter is dated 24 September 1904, and the excerpt begins by saying that the demonstration came out of discussions with Erhard Schmidt during the preceding week, which means that we can safely date the appearance of the axiom of choice and the demonstration of the well-ordering theorem to September 1904.
Brief as it was, Zermelo’s paper gave rise to what is presumably the most lively discussion among mathematicians on the validity, or acceptability, of a mathematical axiom that has ever taken place. Within a couple of years, written contributions to this discussion were published by Felix Bernstein, Schoenflies, Hamel, Hessenberg, and Hausdorff in Germany; Baire, Borel, Hadamard, Lebesgue, Richard, and Poincaré in France; Hobson, Hardy, Jourdain, and Russell in England; Julius König in Hungary; Peano in Italy, and Brouwer in the Netherlands.
6
Zermelo responded to those of these contributions that were critical, which was a majority, in a second paper from 1908. This second paper also contains a new proof of the well-ordering theorem, less intuitive or less perspicuous, it has to be admitted, than the original proof, as well as a new formulation of the axiom of choice, a formulation which will play a crucial role in the following considerations.

data.title: OxCaml - a set of extensions to the OCaml programming language.
data.author: lairv
data.article_summary:
OxCaml 是 OCaml 编程语言的一套快速发展的扩展，由 Jane Street 开发，旨在提升 OCaml 在性能导向编程中的表现。OxCaml 的设计目标是提供安全、便捷、可预测的控制，特别是在性能关键的程序行为方面，且仅在需要时引入复杂性。它保持与 OCaml 的兼容性，所有有效的 OCaml 程序也是有效的 OxCaml 程序。

OxCaml 的扩展包括：
1. **无畏并发**：通过类型系统静态排除数据竞争。
2. **内存布局**：允许指定数据在内存中的布局，并支持 SIMD 处理器扩展。
3. **控制分配**：提供工具减少垃圾回收压力，提高缓存效率和确定性。
4. **生活质量改进**：如多态参数、包含函子、标记元组和不可变数组。

OxCaml 是开源的，但其扩展不保证稳定性或向后兼容性。它提供了与标准 OCaml 工具集兼容的修改版本，方便用户使用。Jane Street 还开源了一些库和工具，部分扩展仅在 OxCaml 中可用。

• Lyngbakr：关注OCaml在高频交易等低延迟场景中的垃圾回收（GC）问题，担心GC暂停会影响性能。他提到了一个相关的播客讨论，其中探讨了OCaml的性能考量。

• avsm：提供了在尝试新opam switch时解决报警问题的实用方法，通过设置环境变量来避免安装包时出现不必要的错误。

• dingdingdang：习惯于使用Golang的VSCode插件，希望OCaml也能与之集成，使设置更简单。

44268782.article_content:
OxCaml
OxCaml is a fast-moving set of extensions to the OCaml programming language.
It is both Jane Street’s production compiler, as well as a laboratory for experiments focused towards making
OCaml better for performance-oriented programming. Our hope is that these extensions can over time be
contributed to upstream OCaml.
OxCaml’s primary design goals are:
to provide
safe, convenient, predictable
control over performance-critical
aspects
of
program behavior
but
only where you need it,
and…
in OCaml!
Let’s talk about what this means!
OxCaml’s extensions are meant to make OCaml a great language for performance engineering. Performance
engineering
requires control, and we want that control to be:
Safe. Safety is a critical feature for making programmers more productive, and for shipping correct
code.
Languages that are pervasively unsafe are too hard to use correctly.
Convenient. We want to provide control without bewildering programmers, or drowning them in endless
annotations.
To achieve this, we aim to maintain OCaml’s excellent type-inference, even as we add considerable
expressiveness
to the type-system.
Predictable. One of the great features of OCaml today is that it’s pretty easy to look at OCaml code and
understand how it’s going to perform. We want our extensions to maintain and improve on that property,
by
making
key performance details explicit at the type-level.
By "only where you need it", we mean that OxCaml’s extensions should be pay-as-you-go. While OxCaml aims to
provide
more power to optimize, you shouldn’t need to swallow extra complexity when you’re not using that power.
By "in OCaml", we mean that all valid OCaml programs are also valid OxCaml programs. But our more profound
goal
is
for OxCaml to feel like OCaml evolving into a better version of itself, rather than a new language. For
that,
OxCaml
needs to honor OCaml’s basic design sensibility, and to preserve the safety, ease, and productivity that are
hallmarks of the language.
OxCaml’s extensions
Our extensions can be roughly organized into a few areas:
Fearless concurrency
Writing correct concurrent programs is notoriously difficult. OxCaml includes additions to the
type
system to
statically rule out data races.
Layouts
OxCaml lets programmers specify the way their data is laid out in memory. It also provides native
access
to
SIMD processor extensions.
Control over allocation
OxCaml gives programmers tools to control allocations, reducing GC pressure and making programs
more
cache efficient and deterministic.
Quality of life
OxCaml also contains some extensions that aren’t specifically about systems programming, but
which
we’ve
found helpful in our day-to-day work:
Polymorphic parameters
Include functor
Labeled tuples
Immutable arrays
Using OxCaml
OxCaml is open-source, and we’re excited to welcome experimental users, especially researchers and tinkerers
who
can
kick the tires and provide feedback on the system. We put the emphasis on experimental because OxCaml makes
no
promises of stability or backwards compatibility for its extensions (though it does remain backwards
compatible
with
OCaml).
OxCaml is intended to be easy to use, and to that end comes with modified versions of the standard OCaml
tool-set,
including:
Package management, compatible with dune and opam
Editor integration via the LSP-server
Source code formatting
Documentation generation
Jane Street has long open sourced a bunch of useful libraries and tools. These are now released in two forms:
one
for
upstream OCaml, in which our extensions have been stripped, and one for OxCaml, where the extensions are
fully
leveraged.
Not all extensions are erasable, so some libraries will be available only for OxCaml. We’ll export
OCaml-compatible
versions of these libraries when the necessary extensions are integrated upstream.
44268782.article_summary:
OxCaml 是 OCaml 编程语言的一套快速发展的扩展，由 Jane Street 开发，旨在提升 OCaml 在性能导向编程中的表现。OxCaml 的设计目标是提供安全、便捷、可预测的控制，特别是在性能关键的程序行为方面，且仅在需要时引入复杂性。它保持与 OCaml 的兼容性，所有有效的 OCaml 程序也是有效的 OxCaml 程序。

OxCaml 的扩展包括：
1. **无畏并发**：通过类型系统静态排除数据竞争。
2. **内存布局**：允许指定数据在内存中的布局，并支持 SIMD 处理器扩展。
3. **控制分配**：提供工具减少垃圾回收压力，提高缓存效率和确定性。
4. **生活质量改进**：如多态参数、包含函子、标记元组和不可变数组。

OxCaml 是开源的，但其扩展不保证稳定性或向后兼容性。它提供了与标准 OCaml 工具集兼容的修改版本，方便用户使用。Jane Street 还开源了一些库和工具，部分扩展仅在 OxCaml 中可用。

data.title: Geometry from Quantum Temporal Correlations
data.author: ljosifov
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了欧几里得三维空间如何从量子时间关联结构中独特出现，特别是通过在一个量子比特上依次测量保罗利可观察量。研究表明，这些量子时间关联与初始状态无关，允许观察者无需了解初始条件即可提取几何数据。这暗示空间可能从量子时间关联中涌现，并提出了一种假设现象的玩具模型。文章4页，无图。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于量子波动如何导致洛伦兹签名和时间维度出现的讨论，以及该理论的可信度和具体论证的争议。

不同观点：
• magicalhippo：介绍了一个关于通过量子波动从均匀4D度量中产生洛伦兹签名和时间维度的理论，提到在引入不对称“噪声”后，一个维度在度量中发生有效符号翻转，从而产生我们熟知的时空度量签名。他自认为只是个门外汉，对细节不予置评，但觉得这个理论听起来很有趣。

• patcon：对内容无法做出专业评估，但对讨论表示好奇。他指出第二作者是学术界非常有名的人物，提供了一些社会证明。他还提到了Sabine Hossenfelder对该论文的视频讲解。

• stared：对该理论表示怀疑。首先，对“理论物理学界对时空不是原始概念的共识正在增加”这一说法提出质疑，认为这一说法过于武断，并没有实际的共识。其次，对使用Pauli矩阵来论证1+3时空的合理性表示质疑，认为这可能是一种循环论证。

• ljosifov：提到Vlatko Vedral（该理论的作者之一）在皇家学会的一个演讲，并提供了一个视频链接，表示自己现在更习惯于一边看视频一边阅读文字稿。

• tomrod：表示对空间是量子层面的相关互动的观点不太理解，但觉得这个理论很有趣。他还提到一个附带的想法，希望有一种基于LLM的工具，可以帮助用户在阅读学术文献时深入理解概念，因为学术写作通常很简洁且引用先前文献，导致快速上手需要大量努力。

• nyeah：询问是否有物理学家愿意评论，特别提到Pauli矩阵是用来处理三个空间轴的，质疑该论文是否有更多内容。

• neom：提到在Hacker News上看到的一篇长文，讨论Jaeger等人的意识理论，其中提到许多“内置”结构是涌现的，认知系统从底层复杂性中生成意义，而不是简单地遵循一套规则。宏观层面的“给定条件”（如几何）可以从深层的非经典过程中涌现出来，类似于“程序生成的量子现实”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该理论的可信度和论证方式，尤其是关于“理论物理学界对时空的共识”的说法和使用Pauli矩阵论证时空结构的合理性。
• 讨论中提到了多位学术权威和相关视频资源，显示出对该理论背后研究者的信任和关注。
• tomrod提出的关于学术文献理解工具的想法引发了对学术写作和学习曲线的讨论。
• neom提到的意识理论提供了一个更广泛的背景，将该讨论与更广泛的哲学和科学问题联系起来。

Title:
Geometry from quantum temporal correlations
Authors:
James Fullwood
,
Vlatko Vedral
View a PDF of the paper titled Geometry from quantum temporal correlations, by James Fullwood and Vlatko Vedral
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
In this work, we show how Euclidean 3-space uniquely emerges from the structure of quantum temporal correlations associated with sequential measurements of Pauli observables on a single qubit. Quite remarkably, the quantum temporal correlations which give rise to geometry are independent of the initial state of the qubit, which we show enables an observer to extract geometric data from sequential measurements without the observer having any knowledge of initial conditions. Such results suggest the plausibility that space itself may emerge from quantum temporal correlations, and we formulate a toy model of such a hypothetical phenomenon.

data.title: Show HN: Qrkey – Offline private key backup on paper
data.author: techwolf12
data.article_summary: **qrkey** 是一个命令行工具，用于生成和恢复用于离线私钥备份的二维码。它可以将文件转换为可打印或存储的二维码，并支持通过扫描二维码恢复文件。对于大文件，它会自动分割为多个二维码，并包含元数据以便于恢复和验证。用户可以通过 Homebrew 或 Docker 安装该工具，并使用简单命令生成和恢复文件。该项目采用 MIT 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过打印存储和恢复私钥等敏感信息的安全性与技术实现

不同观点：
• krunck认为在办公环境的打印设备上打印敏感信息存在风险，因为这些设备可能会在硬盘上存储打印作业数据，技术人员可以访问这些数据。
• RamRodification对命令输入文件的格式提出了疑问，指出生成QR码的命令输出PDF，但恢复文件的命令却接受"file.txt"作为输入，质疑这是否是笔误。
• cornstalks提到想结合Shamir’s secret sharing将私钥分发给家人，以防意外过世时家人可以获取其财务账户，但面临家人不懂技术的挑战。
• vorgol提供了有关纸张存储的讨论链接，供进一步参考。
• slig关注打印私钥时可能存在的打印机软件、固件和联网带来的安全漏洞。
• hypeatei质疑为什么简单的命令行工具需要Docker镜像，认为通常git clone足够，特别是Go语言编写的应用。
• kardianos分享了自己开发的类似工具，用于Keepass数据库的打印存储，并提供了工具链接。
• saclark11提到了PaperAge这个加密解决方案，用于安全地物理备份小秘密，但指出需要确保不忘记密码或在其他地方备份密码。
• qualeed对使用QR码而非直接打印可读文档的优点感到困惑，认为可能缺少明确的用例说明。
• thayne表示这个想法不错，但由于没有打印机且不愿意将私钥交给公共计算机和打印机，因此对自己不实用。
• _whiteCaps_分享了自己类似的设置，使用特定分辨率打印到相纸以获得高质量输出，并提供了项目链接。

qrkey
is a command-line tool for generating and recovering QR codes from files for offline private key backup.
It allows you to convert files into QR codes that can be printed or stored, and later recovered from those QR codes.

data.title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents Against Prompt Injections
data.author: simonw
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一份由多位作者（包括IBM、Invariant Labs、ETH Zurich、Google和Microsoft的专家）撰写的新论文，主题是如何通过设计模式保护大型语言模型（LLM）代理免受提示注入攻击。文章介绍了六种设计模式，包括动作选择模式、计划执行模式、LLM Map-Reduce模式、双LLM模式、代码执行模式和上下文最小化模式。这些模式通过限制代理执行任意任务的能力，有效减轻提示注入的风险。作者强调，当前的LLM技术难以提供绝对的安全保障，因此需要在代理的实用性和安全性之间做出权衡。文章还指出，任何暴露于潜在恶意输入的代理都应被严格限制，以防止触发任何可能影响系统或环境的安全性与机密性的操作。总体而言，这些设计模式为应对提示注入问题提供了现实可行的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLM（大型语言模型）代理中的提示注入（prompt injection）问题及其解决方案的讨论，包括不同的技术设计模式和安全措施。

不同观点：
• **simonw**：强调了在LLM代理中限制不可信输入触发重大操作的重要性，特别是当这些代理与工具和MCP服务器连接时。认为这是当前关键的安全问题。

• **potatolicious**：认为一些设计模式可以结合使用，例如"Plan-Then-Execute"与"Dual LLM"结合，通过使用符号数据存储和变量隔离来增强安全性，从而更好地防御提示注入。

• **fcatalan**：分享了个人实验经历，指出在构建饮食建议代理时，LLM（gemini2.5）意外地限制了对话的范围，尽管提示中没有明确要求这种限制。这表明LLM可能自行施加了一些规则。

• **ntonozzi**：认为当前的限制性方法过于局限，建议改变约束，例如在软件代理中运行容器，限制调用以防止数据泄露，并通过审查拉取请求来增加安全性。

• **mooreds**：提供论文链接，供进一步参考，但没有深入讨论具体观点。

• **swyx**：赞赏论文的实用性和案例研究，指出所有方案都涉及减少代理的“自主性”以换取安全。同时担心能力最大化与效率/安全之间的权衡，通常能力最大化在产品采用和营销中占优。

• **ofirg**：提出"上下文最小化模式"可能存在的问题，例如将注入复制到查询文本中，建议使用类似SQL参数化查询的方法来解决。

• **JSR_FDED**：赞同ofirg的观点，将提示注入防御与SQL参数化查询进行类比。

• **deadbabe**：提出法律层面的讨论，询问是否应对提示注入行为进行法律追责，类似于SQL注入攻击的法律后果。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术解决方案，如"Plan-Then-Execute"、"Dual LLM"、符号数据存储和变量隔离等，旨在通过不同方式增强LLM代理的安全性。
• 争议焦点之一是安全措施的实施是否过于局限，影响了代理的功能和用户体验。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是能力最大化与安全性之间的权衡，以及如何在实际应用中实现这一平衡。
• 最后，法律责任的讨论引出了一个新维度，即提示注入可能带来的法律后果。

Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
13th June 2025
This new paper by 11 authors from organizations including IBM, Invariant Labs, ETH Zurich, Google and Microsoft is an
excellent
addition to the literature on prompt injection and LLM security.
In this work, we describe a number of
design patterns
for LLM agents that significantly mitigate the risk of prompt injections. These design patterns constrain the actions of agents to explicitly prevent them from solving
arbitrary
tasks. We believe these design patterns offer a valuable trade-off between agent utility and security.
Here’s the full citation:
Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
(2025) by Luca Beurer-Kellner, Beat Buesser, Ana-Maria Creţu, Edoardo Debenedetti, Daniel Dobos, Daniel Fabian, Marc Fischer, David Froelicher, Kathrin Grosse, Daniel Naeff, Ezinwanne Ozoani, Andrew Paverd, Florian Tramèr, and Václav Volhejn.
I’m so excited to see papers like this starting to appear. I
wrote about
Google DeepMind’s
Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
paper (aka the CaMeL paper) back in April, which was the first paper I’d seen that proposed a credible solution to some of the challenges posed by prompt injection against tool-using LLM systems (often referred to as “agents”).
This new paper provides a robust explanation of prompt injection, then proposes six design patterns to help protect against it, including the pattern proposed by the CaMeL paper.
The scope of the problem
The Action-Selector Pattern
The Plan-Then-Execute Pattern
The LLM Map-Reduce Pattern
The Dual LLM Pattern
The Code-Then-Execute Pattern
The Context-Minimization pattern
The case studies
Closing thoughts
The scope of the problem
The authors of this paper
very clearly
understand the scope of the problem:
As long as both agents and their defenses rely on the current class of language models,
we believe it is unlikely that general-purpose agents can provide meaningful and reliable safety guarantees
.
This leads to a more productive question:
what kinds of agents can we build
today
that produce useful work while offering resistance to prompt injection attacks?
In this section, we introduce a set of design patterns for LLM agents that aim to mitigate — if not entirely eliminate — the risk of prompt injection attacks. These patterns impose intentional constraints on agents, explicitly limiting their ability to perform
arbitrary
tasks.
This is a very realistic approach. We don’t have a magic solution to prompt injection, so we need to make trade-offs. The trade-off they make here is “limiting the ability of agents to perform arbitrary tasks”. That’s not a popular trade-off, but it gives this paper a lot of credibility in my eye.
This paragraph proves that they fully get it (emphasis mine):
The design patterns we propose share a common guiding principle:
once an LLM agent has ingested untrusted input, it must be constrained so that it is
impossible
for that input to trigger any consequential actions
—that is, actions with negative side effects on the system or its environment. At a minimum, this means that restricted agents must not be able to invoke tools that can break the integrity or confidentiality of the system. Furthermore, their outputs should not pose downstream risks — such as exfiltrating sensitive information (e.g., via embedded links) or manipulating future agent behavior (e.g., harmful responses to a user query).
The way I think about this is that any exposure to potentially malicious tokens entirely taints the output for that prompt. Any attacker who can sneak in their tokens should be considered to have complete control over what happens next—which means they control not just the textual output of the LLM but also any tool calls that the LLM might be able to invoke.
Let’s talk about their design patterns.
The Action-Selector Pattern
A relatively simple pattern that makes agents immune to prompt injections — while still allowing them to take external actions — is to prevent any feedback from these actions back into the agent.
Agents can trigger tools, but cannot be exposed to or act on the responses
from
those tools. You can’t read an email or retrieve a web page, but you can trigger actions such as “send the user to this web page” or “display this message to the user”.
They summarize this pattern as an “LLM-modulated switch statement”, which feels accurate to me.
The Plan-Then-Execute Pattern
A more permissive approach is to allow feedback from tool outputs back to the agent, but to prevent the tool outputs from
influencing
the choice of actions taken by the agent.
The idea here is to plan the tool calls in advance before any chance of exposure to untrusted content. This allows for more sophisticated sequences of actions, without the risk that one of those actions might introduce malicious instructions that then trigger unplanned harmful actions later on.

data.title: The Missing Manual for Signals: State Management for Python Developers
data.author: buibuibui
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种用于Python中的响应式状态管理工具——`reaktiv`，并讨论了何时需要使用这种工具。传统的状态管理方式在处理多组件状态同步或维护手动协调时可能变得复杂且容易出错。文章指出，当状态变化需要在多个组件中传递，或手动更新变得难以维护时，响应式编程（如信号系统）可以有效解决这些问题。

文章详细分析了传统状态管理的弊端，如隐式依赖、紧密耦合、不一致状态窗口和测试复杂性等问题，并提出了响应式状态管理（信号）的解决方案。信号通过显式依赖关系图自动处理状态更新，避免了手动维护带来的潜在错误。

本文还提供了在现有系统中逐步采用信号的方法、常见模式与反模式，以及性能和测试方面的考虑。最终，文章帮助开发者判断何时应采用响应式状态管理，何时则不必。

44267705.article_content:
A practical guide to reactive state management in Python
Introduction
I maintain
reaktiv
. When I demo it to Python teams, I get the same response: "Why do I need this? I can just call functions when things change."
Fair question. Python has excellent patterns for coordinating state changes. You can trigger updates manually, use the observer pattern, or set up event systems. Most Python applications handle state coordination just fine.
But some don't.
If you're building systems where state changes cascade through multiple components, where derived values need to stay synchronized, or where manual coordination is becoming a maintenance burden - signals might solve real problems for you.
Frontend developers recognize the pattern immediately. They've dealt with forgetting to trigger updates when state changes, or having component state get out of sync. Signals solve the "forgot to update X when Y changed" class of bugs.
This manual shows you when that coordination problem is worth solving with reactive programming, and when it's not.
What You'll Learn
When reactive state management solves real problems (and when it doesn't)
How to adopt signals incrementally in existing systems
Patterns that work in production Python applications
Let's start with what breaks as state coordination scales.

The Problem with Traditional State Management
As developers, we've all written variations of this code:
class OrderService:
def __init__(self):
self.orders = []
self.total_revenue = 0.0
self.daily_stats = {}
self.notification_service = NotificationService()
self.analytics_service = AnalyticsService()
def add_order(self, order):
self.orders.append(order)
self.total_revenue += order.amount
self._update_daily_stats(order)
self._send_notifications(order)
self._track_analytics(order)
def _update_daily_stats(self, order):
date = order.created_at.date()
if date not in self.daily_stats:
self.daily_stats[date] = {"count": 0, "revenue": 0.0}
self.daily_stats[date]["count"] += 1
self.daily_stats[date]["revenue"] += order.amount
def _send_notifications(self, order):
if order.amount > 1000:
self.notification_service.send_high_value_alert(order)
if len(self.orders) % 100 == 0:
self.notification_service.send_milestone_alert(len(self.orders))
def _track_analytics(self, order):
self.analytics_service.track_order(order)
if self.total_revenue > 50000:
self.analytics_service.track_milestone("revenue_50k")

Every time we add an order, we must remember to update:
Total revenue

Notifications

Any future derived state
Miss one update? Silent bugs. Add a new derived value? Modify every entry point.
2.
Implicit Dependencies
The relationship between orders and derived state is buried in imperative code. New developers (or future you) must trace through method calls to understand what depends on what.
3.

Between the moment

44267705.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种用于Python中的响应式状态管理工具——`reaktiv`，并讨论了何时需要使用这种工具。传统的状态管理方式在处理多组件状态同步或维护手动协调时可能变得复杂且容易出错。文章指出，当状态变化需要在多个组件中传递，或手动更新变得难以维护时，响应式编程（如信号系统）可以有效解决这些问题。

文章详细分析了传统状态管理的弊端，如隐式依赖、紧密耦合、不一致状态窗口和测试复杂性等问题，并提出了响应式状态管理（信号）的解决方案。信号通过显式依赖关系图自动处理状态更新，避免了手动维护带来的潜在错误。

本文还提供了在现有系统中逐步采用信号的方法、常见模式与反模式，以及性能和测试方面的考虑。最终，文章帮助开发者判断何时应采用响应式状态管理，何时则不必。

data.article_summary: Anker正在召回超过110万个PowerCore 10000型号的充电宝，由于其锂离子电池存在过热、起火和爆炸风险。这些产品通过亚马逊、Newegg和eBay等网站在2016年6月至2022年12月间售出。公司已收到19起相关事故报告，造成轻微烧伤和超过60,700美元的财产损失。召回范围包括特定序列号的美国销售产品。消费者可选择30美元礼品卡或免费更换升级版充电宝（型号A1388）。召回程序要求提交包含日期、“recall”字样、型号和序列号的照片，并妥善处理旧充电宝以防火灾风险。建议检查产品是否在召回之列并联系Anker进行更换。

News
Anker is recalling over 1.1 million power banks due to fire and burn risks
﻿Stop using the Anker PowerCore 10000 power banks immediately and contact the company for a free replacement.
﻿Stop using the Anker PowerCore 10000 power banks immediately and contact the company for a free replacement.
by
Andrew Liszewski
Jun 12, 2025, 3:19 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads

See our ethics statement.
The recalled power bank was sold several years ago through sites like Amazon, Newegg, and eBay.
Image: Anker
Andrew Liszewski
is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.
Anker has
issued a recall for its PowerCore 10000 power bank
(model A1263) due to a “potential issue with the lithium-ion battery” that could pose a fire safety risk. The company has received 19 reports of fires and explosions that have caused minor burn injuries and resulted in property damage totaling over $60,700,
according to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (USCPSC)
.
The recall covers about 1,158,000 units that were sold online through Amazon, Newegg, and eBay between June 2016 and December 2022. The affected batteries can be identified by the Anker logo engraved on the side with the model number A1263 printed on the bottom edge. However, Anker is only recalling units sold in the US with qualifying serial numbers. To check if yours is included, you’ll need to
visit Anker’s website
.
The power bank’s model and serial numbers can be found on its bottom edge, while the Anker logo is engraved on the side.
Image: Anker
Anker is offering affected consumers their choice of either a $30 gift card (the recalled battery cost around $27) that can be used on
Anker.com
, or a free 10,000mAh Anker power bank as a replacement (model A1388) featuring upgrades including a charge level display and a USB-C charging cable lanyard.
To receive the gift card or the replacement, Anker requires a “photo of the power bank with the submission date and the word ‘recall’ or ‘recalled’ written clearly in permanent marker,” to be submitted, and a “photo showing the model number and serial number (SN) printed on the bottom of the device.” The company is also requesting a purchase receipt, but it’s not mandatory to participate in the recall.
After confirming that your power bank is one of the recalled units, Anker says it should be taken to a facility that can safely dispose of lithium-ion batteries due to the risk of fire. Those facilities can be found through the
Environmental Protection Agency’s website
or
other organizations
in the US that specialize in processing e-waste. Do not throw them in the trash, recycling bins, or used battery boxes provided at various retail locations.
The recall is also a reminder that power banks and backup batteries can potentially develop severe issues over time, as these particular units are almost a decade old. If you’ve been regularly using devices featuring lithium-ion batteries for a while, you’ll want to be mindful of issues like overheating or visible swelling and dispose of them properly if you think there’s a potential problem. And while the technology is currently more expensive than lithium-ion batteries, you can also
consider upgrading to solid-state batteries
which are more powerful, safer, and
longer lasting than what we commonly use now
to power our devices.

data.title: Corporations as Paperclip Maximizers
data.author: busssard
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过将企业、生物系统和错位的AI进行类比，探讨它们在优化过程中如何因核心目标（利润、食物、电力）而产生与人类价值观冲突的行为。企业如同生物体，依赖持续的收入来维持运作，这种需求如同生物需要食物或AI需要电力，是不可妥协的。文章建议，通过将企业视为具有内在目标的系统，可以借鉴AI对齐研究的方法，调整企业行为以符合社会福祉。文章还讨论了历史上的自动化趋势、企业错位问题，以及如合作社和非政府组织等替代组织模式，提出重新设计企业激励机制的策略。通过理解企业作为“有机体”的特性，可以帮助监管机构和研究人员更好地确保企业行为与社会目标一致。
